article_content: In a shocking incident, a 65-year-old Tennessee man, Dale Farris, has been charged with aggravated assault and reckless endangerment after shooting a teenager who was participating in a prank involving toilet paper. The teenager, who was armed with nothing but toilet paper, was struck by multiple pellets from Farris' gun, sustaining injuries to his foot, knee, palm, thigh, and torso. Despite the severity of the situation, the teenager's injuries were not life-threatening. The incident occurred on October 20 when a group of teens, including some students from Huntland School, where Principal Ken Bishop is the head, decided to toilet paper the principal's yard as a prank. Farris, who lives nearby, emerged from his residence and fired at least two shots at the group, hitting one of the teenagers. The authorities have stated that the teens were not on Farris' property and were not causing any harm to his property at the time of the shooting. Farris has been released from custody after posting a $125,000 bond and is due to appear in court on December 5. The incident has raised questions about vigilantism and the appropriate response to perceived threats.
